# 4. Import shotgun metagenomic data and create phyloseq object - with MetaPhlan
```{r}
tax_table_ra <- read.delim("Supplementary_table3.txt", skip = 1)

tax_table_M_abs <- read.delim("Supplementary_table4.txt")
tax_table_C_abs <- read.delim("Supplementary_table5.txt")

tax_table_M_abs = tax_table_M_abs[, -2] #remove clade id
tax_table_C_abs = tax_table_C_abs[, -2] #remove clade id

tax_table_abs <- full_join(tax_table_M_abs, tax_table_C_abs, by = "clade_name") #Join both mother and child table
tax_table_abs[is.na(tax_table_abs)] <- 0

# Erase data frames and vectors that are not necessary anymore
  rm("tax_table_M_abs", "tax_table_C_abs")
```

## 4.1 Relative abundance
```{r}
# Create a taxonomy table - relative abundances
  # Obtain a table with only the tax names
  tax_names_ra <- str_split_fixed(tax_table_ra$clade_name, "\\|[p,c,o,f,g,s,t]__", 8)
  tax_names_ra <- as.data.frame(tax_names_ra)
  tax_names_ra[,1] <- str_remove(tax_names_ra[,1], "k__")
  # Keeping only the rows with the complete taxonomy
  tax_names_ra <- tax_names_ra[-(which(tax_names_ra[,8] == "")),]
  # Changing colnames
  colnames(tax_names_ra) <- c("Kingdom", "Phylum", "Class","Order","Family","Genus","Species", "SGB")
  # Adding the rownames
  tax_names_ra <- tax_names_ra %>%
    mutate(ASV = paste("SGB", seq(1:nrow(tax_names_ra)), sep=""))
  rownames(tax_names_ra) <- tax_names_ra$ASV
  asv_num <- tax_names_ra$ASV
  tax_names_ra <- tax_names_ra[,-9]
  tax_names_ra <- as.matrix(tax_names_ra) #We have now a taxonomy table, similar than the one obtain with DADA2
  # Set as tax table phyloseq object
  taxonomy_table_ra <- tax_table(tax_names_ra)


# Abundance table - relative abundances
  abun_table_ra <- cbind(str_split_fixed(tax_table_ra$clade_name, "\\|[p,c,o,f,g,s,t]__", 8),tax_table_ra)
  abun_table_ra <- as.data.frame(abun_table_ra)
  abun_table_ra[,1] <- str_remove(abun_table_ra[,1], "k__")
  abun_table_ra <- abun_table_ra[-(which(abun_table_ra[,8] == "")),] 
  rownames(abun_table_ra) <- asv_num
  abun_table_ra <- abun_table_ra[,-c(1:9)]
  # We have now a table with the column being each sample
  # The row are the ASV assigned to a bacteria in the taxonomy table
  
  # Clear the column name
  colnames(abun_table_ra) <- str_remove(colnames(abun_table_ra), "_metaphlan")
  # Extract columns names to add as metadata later
  column_names <- data.frame(ColumnNames = colnames(abun_table_ra))
  colnames(abun_table_ra) <- str_remove(colnames(abun_table_ra), "r") #That was useful for sequencing to know which tube to use, it stood for "redone" when there was not enough DNA. We can remove it now
  colnames(abun_table_ra) <- str_remove(colnames(abun_table_ra), "t") #That was useful for sequencing to know which tube to use, it stood for "topup" when there was not enough DNA. We can remove it now
  
  # Set as otu_table phyloseq object
  abun_table_ra <- as.matrix(abun_table_ra)
  class(abun_table_ra) <- "numeric"
  abundance_table_ra = otu_table(abun_table_ra, taxa_are_rows = TRUE)

# We have now a tax table and an otu table, we can create our phyloseq
  physeq_ra <- phyloseq(taxonomy_table_ra, abundance_table_ra)
  get_taxa_unique(physeq_ra, "Kingdom")

# Add metadata to phyloseq object
  rownames(metadata_df) <- metadata_df$NovogeneID
  metadata = sample_data(metadata_df)
  
  physeq_ra <- merge_phyloseq(physeq_ra, metadata)
  head(sample_data(physeq_ra))
  
# Create a dataframe with the abundance of each bacteria in the samples and the taxonomy
  abun_table_ra_df <- as.data.frame(abun_table_ra) %>%
      mutate(rows = rownames(.)) %>% 
        left_join(as.data.frame(tax_names_ra) %>% mutate(rows = rownames(.)), by = "rows") %>%
          dplyr::select(-rows)
  
# Phyloseq object description
  physeq_ra # 2445 taxa
  
# Add SequencingID to metadata
  # Add a new column 'NovogeneID' based on 'ColumnNames', removing 'r' or 't' at the end
  column_names$NovogeneID <- ifelse(
    grepl("[rt]$", column_names$ColumnNames),  # Check if 'ColumnNames' ends with 'r' or 't'
    sub("[rt]$", "", column_names$ColumnNames), # Remove the trailing 'r' or 't' if it exists
    column_names$ColumnNames                    # Otherwise, keep the original value
  )

# Erase data frames and vectors that are not necessary anymore
  rm("column_names", "today_date", "output_path", "tax_names_ra", "abun_table_ra", "asv_num", "tax_table_ra")
```

## 4.2 Reads number (~ Absolute abundances)
```{r}
# Create a taxonomy table - reads number (absolute abundances)
  # Obtain a table with only the tax names
  tax_names_abs <- str_split_fixed(tax_table_abs$clade_name, "\\|[p,c,o,f,g,s,t]__", 8)
  tax_names_abs <- as.data.frame(tax_names_abs)
  tax_names_abs[,1] <- str_remove(tax_names_abs[,1], "k__")
  # Keeping only the rows with the complete taxonomy
  tax_names_abs <- tax_names_abs[-(which(tax_names_abs[,8] == "")),]
  # Changing colnames
  colnames(tax_names_abs) <- c("Kingdom", "Phylum", "Class","Order","Family","Genus","Species", "SGB")
  # Adding the rownames
  tax_names_abs <- tax_names_abs %>%
    mutate(ASV_abs = paste("SGB", seq(1:nrow(tax_names_abs)), sep=""))
  rownames(tax_names_abs) <- tax_names_abs$ASV_abs
  asv_num_abs <- tax_names_abs$ASV_abs
  tax_names_abs_df = tax_names_abs #this is created for later use with the clustering and heatmap
  tax_names_abs <- tax_names_abs[,-9]
  tax_names_abs <- as.matrix(tax_names_abs) #We have now a taxonomy table, similar than the one obtain with DADA2
  # Set as tax table phyloseq object
  taxonomy_table_abs <- tax_table(tax_names_abs)
  
# Abundance table - relative abundances
  abun_table_abs <- cbind(str_split_fixed(tax_table_abs$clade_name, "\\|[p,c,o,f,g,s,t]__", 8),tax_table_abs)
  abun_table_abs <- as.data.frame(abun_table_abs)
  abun_table_abs[,1] <- str_remove(abun_table_abs[,1], "k__")
  abun_table_abs <- abun_table_abs[-(which(abun_table_abs[,8] == "")),] 
  rownames(abun_table_abs) <- asv_num_abs
  abun_table_abs <- abun_table_abs[,-c(1:9)]
  # We have now a table with the column being each sample
  # The row are the ASV assigned to a bacteria in the taxonomy table
  
  # Clear the column name
  colnames(abun_table_abs) <- str_remove(colnames(abun_table_abs), "_metaphlan_profile")
  colnames(abun_table_abs) <- str_remove(colnames(abun_table_abs), "r") #That was useful for sequencing to know which tube to use, it stood for "redone" when there was not enough DNA. We can remove it now
  colnames(abun_table_abs) <- str_remove(colnames(abun_table_abs), "t") #That was useful for sequencing to know which tube to use, it stood for "redone" when there was not enough DNA. We can remove it now
  
  # Set as otu_table phyloseq object
  abun_table_abs <- as.matrix(abun_table_abs)
  class(abun_table_abs) <- "numeric"
  abundance_table_abs = otu_table(abun_table_abs, taxa_are_rows = TRUE)
  
  # We have now a tax table and an otu table, we can create our phyloseq
  physeq_abs <- phyloseq(taxonomy_table_abs, abundance_table_abs)
  get_taxa_unique(physeq_abs, "Kingdom") 
  
# Add metadata to phyloseq object
  rownames(metadata_df) <- metadata_df$NovogeneID
  metadata = sample_data(metadata_df)
  
  physeq_abs <- merge_phyloseq(physeq_abs, metadata)
  head(sample_data(physeq_abs))
    
# Erase data frames and vectors that are not necessary anymore
  rm("tax_names_abs", "abun_table_abs", "asv_num_abs", "tax_table_abs", "metadata")

# Phyloseq object description
  physeq_abs # 2445 taxa
  
```

# 5. Remove eukaryotes and filter phyloseq object
## Remove all eukaryotes
```{r}
# Remove all the eukaryotes from the tax table (keep only bacteria and archea)
  physeq_ra_filt <- subset_taxa(physeq_ra, Kingdom != "Eukaryota")
  physeq_abs_filt <- subset_taxa(physeq_abs, Kingdom != "Eukaryota")

# Transform in relative abundance (again because we've removed eukaryotes)
  physeq_ra_filt <- transform_sample_counts(physeq_ra_filt, function(x) x / sum(x)) 
  physeq_ra_filt # see what is inside now
  # 2434 taxa => 11 taxa were removed corresponding to eukaryota
```

# 6. Top 20 most abundant taxa
Top 20 most abundant taxa and 1 "other" category with the rest of the taxa
```{r}
# Child
  phy_fam = tax_glom(physeq_ra_filt, taxrank = "Family") # 383 families
  phy_fam_C <- subset_samples(phy_fam, individual == "Child")
  # Create phyloseq object of the top 20 families
    TopFam_Ctrl_C <- names(sort(taxa_sums(phy_fam_C), TRUE)[1:20]) #Take the 20 most abundant families in children's samples
    CtrlFam20_C <- prune_taxa(TopFam_Ctrl_C, phy_fam_C) #Create a new phyloseq object containing only the 20 most abundant families
  # Create phyloseq object of other families (from rank 21 to xxx)
    OtherF_Ctrl_C <- names(sort(taxa_sums(phy_fam_C), TRUE)[c(21:383)]) #change here depending on the number of families you initially have
    CtrlF_other_C <- prune_taxa(OtherF_Ctrl_C, phy_fam_C)
    others_otu_C <- t(as.matrix(apply(otu_table(CtrlF_other_C), 2, sum))) #sum the abundance for all the "others" family (not top 20)
    rownames(others_otu_C) <- "Others Families"
    others_otu_C = otu_table(others_otu_C, taxa_are_rows = TRUE) #create an OTU table for phyloseq
    other_taxF_C <- c("Others","Others","Others","Others","Others","Others","Others", "Others") #Put "Others" for each taxonomic rank
    other_taxF_C <- as.matrix(other_taxF_C)
    rownames(other_taxF_C) <- colnames(tax_table(CtrlF_other_C))
    other_taxF_C <- t(other_taxF_C)
    rownames(other_taxF_C) <- "Others Families"
    other_taxF_C =  tax_table(other_taxF_C) #create a tax table for phyloseq
    others_CtrlF_C = phyloseq(others_otu_C,other_taxF_C) #create the phyloseq object
    others_CtrlF_C = merge_phyloseq(sample_data(phy_fam_C), others_CtrlF_C) #add metadata
    others_CtrlF_C
  # Regrouping both phyloseq objects into 1
    ctrlF_C <- merge_phyloseq(CtrlFam20_C, others_CtrlF_C)
    ctrlF_melt_C <- psmelt(ctrlF_C)
  # Get the unique top 20 (+1 = other) families in children
    unique(ctrlF_melt_C$Family)
  
# Mother
  phy_fam = tax_glom(physeq_ra_filt, taxrank = "Family") # 383 families
  phy_fam_M <- subset_samples(phy_fam, individual == "Mother")
  # Create phyloseq object of the top 20 families
    TopFam_Ctrl_M <- names(sort(taxa_sums(phy_fam_M), TRUE)[1:20])
    CtrlFam20_M <- prune_taxa(TopFam_Ctrl_M, phy_fam_M)
  # Create phyloseq object of other families (from rank 21 to xxx)
    OtherF_Ctrl_M <- names(sort(taxa_sums(phy_fam_M), TRUE)[c(21:383)])
    CtrlF_other_M <- prune_taxa(OtherF_Ctrl_M, phy_fam_M)
    others_otu_M <- t(as.matrix(apply(otu_table(CtrlF_other_M), 2, sum))) #sum the abundance for all the "others" family (not top 20)
    rownames(others_otu_M) <- "Others Families"
    others_otu_M = otu_table(others_otu_M, taxa_are_rows = TRUE) #create an OTU table for phyloseq
    other_taxF_M <- c("Others","Others","Others","Others","Others","Others","Others", "Others") #Put "Others" for each taxonomic rank
    other_taxF_M <- as.matrix(other_taxF_M)
    rownames(other_taxF_M) <- colnames(tax_table(CtrlF_other_M))
    other_taxF_M <- t(other_taxF_M)
    rownames(other_taxF_M) <- "Others Families"
    other_taxF_M =  tax_table(other_taxF_M)
    others_CtrlF_M = phyloseq(others_otu_M,other_taxF_M)
    others_CtrlF_M = merge_phyloseq(sample_data(phy_fam_M), others_CtrlF_M)
    others_CtrlF_M
  # Regrouping phyloseq
    ctrlF_M <- merge_phyloseq(CtrlFam20_M, others_CtrlF_M)
    ctrlF_melt_M <- psmelt(ctrlF_M)
  # Get the unique top 20 (+1 = other) families in mothers
    unique(ctrlF_melt_M$Family)

# Remove unwanted objects
rm("phy_fam", "phy_fam_C", "TopFam_Ctrl_C", "CtrlFam20_C", "OtherF_Ctrl_C", "CtrlF_other_C", "others_otu_C", "other_taxF_C", "others_CtrlF_C", "phy_fam_M", "TopFam_Ctrl_M", "CtrlFam20_M", "OtherF_Ctrl_M", "CtrlF_other_M", "others_otu_M", "other_taxF_M", "others_CtrlF_M")

```

# 9. Epidemiological description
## 9.1 Demographic infos
```{r}
# Table
  metadata_df %>%
    filter(Visit == "Inc") %>%
    gtsummary::tbl_summary(
      include = c(all_of(animals), "s90_spec"),
      by = "district_cat", #classif etc (categorie)
      missing_text = "NA",
      #missing = "no",
      statistic = list(all_continuous() ~ "{mean} ({min}-{max})")
    ) %>%
    add_overall(last = TRUE) %>%
    add_p() %>%
    bold_labels()
  
# Plot
  metadata_df %>%
    filter(Visit == "Inc") %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = classif, y = age, color = classif)) +
    geom_boxplot() + 
    theme_bw() +
    scale_color_manual(values = pal_muac) +
    theme(legend.position="bottom", 
          legend.text=element_text(size = 8), 
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) +
    ggtitle("Age") +
    stat_compare_means(label = "p.signif")
  
```

# 11. Alpha diversity

## 11.1 Generate alpha diversity metrics
```{r}
alpha = estimate_richness(physeq_abs_filt)
alpha

# Add alpha diversity metrics to data frame
  NovogeneID <- rownames(alpha)
  rownames(alpha) <- NULL
  alpha <- cbind(NovogeneID,alpha)
  metadata_df = dplyr::left_join(metadata_df, alpha, by = "NovogeneID")
  
# Test if the difference is significant between Mothers and Childrens' samples
  wilcox.test(formula = Shannon ~ individual, data = metadata_df)
  
# Delete unecessary things
  rm("NovogeneID")
```

## 11.2 Alpha diversity of the children and mother stool microbiomes [Boxplots (M+C)]
```{r}
Sha = ggplot(metadata_df, aes(x = individual, y = Shannon, color = individual)) +
            geom_boxplot() + 
            theme_bw() +
            scale_color_manual(values=c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9")) +
            theme(legend.position="bottom", 
                  legend.text=element_text(size = 8), 
                  plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), 
                  axis.title.y=element_blank(),
                  axis.title.x=element_blank(),
                  axis.text.x=element_blank(),
                  axis.ticks.x=element_blank()
                  ) + 
            ggtitle("Shannon index") +
            ggpubr::stat_compare_means(method = "wilcox.test", label.x = 1, label.y = 7, size = 3) +      # Add global p-value
            ggpubr::stat_compare_means(label = "p.signif", method = "wilcox.test")
      
Obs = ggplot(metadata_df, aes(x = individual, y = Observed, color = individual)) +
            geom_boxplot() + #Add p-value from the test below
            scale_color_manual(values=c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9")) +
            theme_bw() +
            theme(legend.position="bottom", 
                  legend.text=element_text(size=8), 
                  plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), 
                  axis.title.y=element_blank(),
                  axis.title.x=element_blank(),
                  axis.text.x=element_blank(),
                  axis.ticks.x=element_blank()
                  ) + 
            ggtitle("Observed index") +
            ggpubr::stat_compare_means(method = "wilcox.test", label.x = 1, label.y = 600, size = 3) +      # Add global p-value
            ggpubr::stat_compare_means(label = "p.signif", method = "wilcox.test")

InvS = ggplot(metadata_df, aes(x = individual, y = InvSimpson, color = individual)) +
              geom_boxplot() + #Add p-value from the test below
              scale_color_manual(values=c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9")) +
              theme_bw() +
              theme(legend.position="bottom", 
                    legend.text=element_text(size=8), 
                    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), 
                    axis.title.y=element_blank(),
                    axis.title.x=element_blank(),
                    axis.text.x=element_blank(),
                    axis.ticks.x=element_blank()
                    ) + 
              ggtitle("Inverse Simpson index") +
              ggpubr::stat_compare_means(method = "wilcox.test", label.x = 1, label.y = 75, size = 3) +      # Add global p-value
              ggpubr::stat_compare_means(label = "p.signif", method = "wilcox.test")

alphadiv = ggarrange(Obs, Sha, InvS, 
             nrow = 1,
             widths = c(1, 1, 1),
             common.legend = TRUE, legend="bottom")

annotate_figure(alphadiv, top = text_grob("Alpha diversity measures",
                                      color = "black", face = "bold", size = 14))

# Delete unecessary things
  rm("Sha", "Obs", "InvS", "alphadiv")
```

# 12. Beta diversity 
Effect of nutritional classification (MUAC) and mode of delivery on the stool microbiome

## 12.1 Generate the distances between the samples (M+C) [PCoA - Beta diversity]
```{r}
# Mother and child together
  dist_bc <- phyloseq::distance(physeq_ra_filt, method = "bray")
  pcoa_br <- ordinate(physeq_ra_filt, "PCoA", dist_bc)

# Children's samples only
# Subset samples first
physeq_child <- subset_samples(physeq_ra_filt, individual == "Child")
  
  # Bray Curtis
    dist_bc_C <- phyloseq::distance(physeq_child, method = "bray")
    pcoa_br_C <- ordinate(physeq_child, method = "PCoA", distance = dist_bc_C)
  
  # Euclidean 
    dist_euc_C <- phyloseq::distance(subset_samples(physeq_ra_filt, individual == "Child"),
                                     method = "euclidean")
    pcoa_euc_C <- ordinate(physeq_ra_filt, "PCoA", dist_euc_C)
```

## 12.3 Beta-dispersion
```{r}
# For the mother by classif - PCoA
ps_m <- subset_samples(physeq_ra_filt, individual == "Mother")
bray_m <- phyloseq::distance(ps_m, method = "bray")

ord_m <- ordinate(ps_m, method = "PCoA", distance = bray_m)

p_m = plot_ordination(ps_m, ord_m, color = "classif") +
  stat_ellipse(position = "identity", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal_muac, name = "Maternal nutritional status") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 10)) +
  ggtitle("Mothers – Bray-Curtis PCoA") +
  annotate("text", x = -0.5, y = 0.5,  # adjust coordinates as needed
           label = paste0("PERMANOVA: R² = 0.01, p = 0.007"), # \nPERMDISP: p = 0.10
           hjust = 0, size = 3)

# For the children by classif - PCoA
ps_c <- subset_samples(physeq_ra_filt, individual == "Child")
bray_c <- phyloseq::distance(ps_c, method = "bray")

ord_c <- ordinate(ps_c, method = "PCoA", distance = bray_c)

p_c = plot_ordination(ps_c, ord_c, color = "classif") +
  stat_ellipse(position = "identity", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal_muac, name = "Maternal nutritional status") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 10)) +
  ggtitle("Children – Bray-Curtis PCoA") +
  annotate("text", x = -0.6, y = 0.6,
           label = paste0("PERMANOVA: R² = 0.01, p = 0.25"), # \nPERMDISP: p = 0.005
           hjust = 0, size = 3)

(p_m | p_c) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# Beta dispersion
meta_m <- sample_data(ps_m)
meta_c <- sample_data(ps_c)

disp_m <- betadisper(bray_m, meta_m$classif)
disp_c <- betadisper(bray_c, meta_c$classif)

# Extract the 6 dispersion values (for both mother and children and for the 3 classif => 6 total)
disp_mothers <- tapply(disp_m$distances,
                       meta_m$classif,
                       mean)

disp_children <- tapply(disp_c$distances,
                        meta_c$classif,
                        mean)

df_m <- data.frame(distance = disp_m$distances, classif = disp_m$group)
df_m$classif <- factor(df_m$classif, levels = c("Overnourished", "Normally nourished", "Undernourished"))
pbox_m <- ggplot(df_m, aes(x = classif, y = distance, fill = classif)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_muac, name = "Maternal nutritional status") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("ON", "NN", "UN")) +
  theme_bw() +
  ggtitle("Beta dispersion – Mothers") +
  xlab("Maternal nutritional status") +
  ylab("Distance to group centroid") +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        plot.title = element_text(size = 10)) + 
  annotate("text", x = 2, y = max(df_m$distance) * 1.05,
           label = paste0("PERMDISP: p = 0.1"), # see below the test and result
           hjust = 0.5, size = 4)

df_c <- data.frame(distance = disp_c$distances, classif = disp_c$group)
df_c$classif <- factor(df_c$classif, levels = c("Overnourished", "Normally nourished", "Undernourished"))
pbox_c <- ggplot(df_c, aes(x = classif, y = distance, fill = classif)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_muac, name = "Maternal nutritional status") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("ON", "NN", "UN")) +
  theme_bw() +
  ggtitle("Beta dispersion – Children") +
  xlab(" Maternal nutritional status") +
  ylab("Distance to group centroid") +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        plot.title = element_text(size = 10)) +
  annotate("text", x = 2, y = max(df_c$distance) * 1.05,
           label = paste0("PERMDISP: p = 0.005"), # see below the test and result
           hjust = 0.5, size = 4)

(pbox_m | pbox_c) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# Statistical test (PERMDISP) 
set.seed(123)
permutest(disp_m) 
set.seed(123)
permutest(disp_c) 

# Statistical test (PERMANOVA) 
meta_m <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_m))
set.seed(123)
perm_m <- adonis2(bray_m ~ classif,
                  data = meta_m,
                  permutations = 999
                  )
perm_m 

meta_c <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_c))
set.seed(123)
perm_c <- adonis2(bray_c ~ classif,
                  data = meta_c,
                  permutations = 999
                  )
perm_c 

# pairwise comparisons
TukeyHSD(disp_m) 
TukeyHSD(disp_c)
```

## 12.6 Get the relative abundance by species and by sample
```{r}
# Get the relative abundance by species and by sample
  abun_ra_sp_df = abun_table_ra_df[, -c(473:478)]
  abun_ra_sp_df = abun_ra_sp_df[, -474]
  
  # Sum abundance values across rows that share the same Species
  abun_ra_sp_df <- abun_ra_sp_df %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Species) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(across(everything(), sum, na.rm = TRUE))
  
  # Pivot longer so we have one abundance per row
  df_long <- abun_ra_sp_df %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = -Species,                  # All columns except 'Species'
                 names_to = "Sample",              # Former column names become 'Sample'
                 values_to = "Abundance"           # Cell values become 'Abundance'
                 )
  
  # Pivot wider to have species as columns
  abun_ra_sp_df <- df_long %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = Species,             # New columns will be the species names
                values_from = Abundance           # Cell values will be the abundance
                )

  # Remove unnecessary objects
  rm("df_long") # rm(abun_table_ra_df)

# Add the relative abundances to the metadata
metadata_abun_df = metadata_df %>%
  left_join(abun_ra_sp_df, by = c("SequencingID" = "Sample"))

```

## 12.7 Envfit to fit variables on the PCoA
The aim here is to test the correlation between the relative abundance (children stool microbiomes) and different variables

### 12.7.1 Family level
```{r}
phy_fam_C = tax_glom(physeq_child, taxrank = "Family")
phy_ra_fam_C <- transform_sample_counts(phy_fam_C, function(x) x / sum(x)) 

OTU_C = as(otu_table(phy_ra_fam_C), "matrix")
otu_C <- as.data.frame(OTU_C)
TAX_C = as(tax_table(phy_ra_fam_C), "matrix")
tax_C <- as.data.frame(TAX_C)
META_C = as(sample_data(phy_ra_fam_C), "matrix")
meta_C <- as.data.frame(META_C)

tax_otu_C <- cbind(tax_C, otu_C)
tax_otu_C$Name <- str_c(tax_otu_C$Kingdom, '_',tax_otu_C$Phylum, '_', tax_otu_C$Class, '_', tax_otu_C$Order, '_', tax_otu_C$Family)
n_distinct(tax_otu_C$Name)
tax_otu_C[, 234] <- as.character(tax_otu_C[, 234])
length(unique(tax_otu_C[,234]))
rownames(tax_otu_C) <- tax_otu_C[,234]
tax_otu_C <- tax_otu_C[,-c(1:8,234)]
tax_otu_C <- t(tax_otu_C)
class(tax_otu_C) <- "numeric"
tax_otu_C <- as.data.frame(tax_otu_C)
dist_C <- vegdist(tax_otu_C[, 1:383],  method = "bray")
PCOA_C <- pcoa(dist_C)
vectorPCOA_C <- cbind(PCOA_C$vectors[, 1:2])

# Arrows and taxa name
env.fit_fam_C <- envfit(vectorPCOA_C, tax_otu_C[,1:383], perm = 999) #Warning: the standard deviation is zero

env.fit_C.sig  <- as.data.frame(scores(env.fit_fam_C, display = "vectors"))
env.fit_C.vect <- as.list(env.fit_fam_C$vectors)
coordinates_C <- cbind(as.data.frame(env.fit_C.vect$arrows*sqrt(env.fit_C.vect$r)), as.data.frame(env.fit_C.vect$pvals))
coordinates_sign_C <- subset(coordinates_C, as.data.frame(env.fit_C.vect$pvals) <= 0.05)
coordinates_sign_C <- cbind(coordinates_sign_C, species = rownames(coordinates_sign_C))
arr_pvals_coord_C <- coordinates_sign_C %>%
  mutate(Coord = (Axis.1*Axis.1)+(Axis.2*Axis.2))
arr_pvals_coord_C[,5] <- as.numeric(arr_pvals_coord_C[,5])
df_envfit_C <- scores(env.fit_fam_C,display=c("vectors"))
df_envfit_C <- df_envfit_C*vegan:::ordiArrowMul(df_envfit_C)
df_envfit_C <- as.data.frame(df_envfit_C)
df_envfit_C$species <- rownames(df_envfit_C)
df_envfit_C <- df_envfit_C %>% 
  filter(species %in% coordinates_sign_C$species)
arrows_names_C <- str_split_fixed(df_envfit_C$species, "_", 5)
arrows_names_C <- as.data.frame(arrows_names_C)
arrows_names_C <- arrows_names_C %>%
  mutate(tax_name = case_when(
    !str_detect(V5, "Unassigned") ~ V5,
    !str_detect(V4, "Unassigned") ~ paste(V4, V5),
    !str_detect(V3, "Unassigned") ~ paste(V3, V5),
    str_detect(V3, "Unassigned") ~ paste(V2, V5),
    TRUE ~ V5
  ))
df_envfit_C <- df_envfit_C %>% 
  mutate(tax_name = arrows_names_C$tax_name)

# Plotting
ft.scores_C <- as.data.frame(vectorPCOA_C)
ft.scores_C$fastqID <- rownames(tax_otu_C)
which(rownames(meta_C) != rownames(ft.scores_C))


ft.scores_C$classif <- meta_C$classif
ft.scores_C$howborn_combined <- meta_C$howborn_combined
ft.scores_C$district_cat <- meta_C$district_cat
ft.scores_C <- distinct(ft.scores_C)

per_explained_C <- 100*PCOA_C$values$Relative_eig / sum(PCOA_C$values$Relative_eig)
per_explained_C <- round(per_explained_C[1:2], digits = 1)
labs_C <- c(glue("Axis1 [{per_explained_C[1]}%]"),
          glue("Axis2 [{per_explained_C[2]}%]"))


ggplot() +
   geom_point(data = ft.scores_C,
              aes(x = Axis.1, y = Axis.2,
                  color = classif, shape = howborn_combined),
              size = 3, show.legend = TRUE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal_muac, name = "Nutritional categorie (MUAC)") +
  scale_shape_manual(limits = c("Vaginally", "C-section"), values=c(15:16), name = "Mode of delivery") +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = df_envfit_C$Axis.1*0.5,yend = df_envfit_C$Axis.2*0.5),
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm")),color="#808080",alpha=0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(df_envfit_C$Axis.1*0.52, df_envfit_C$Axis.2*0.52, label = df_envfit_C$tax_name, fontface=3), color="#303030",alpha=0.5, size=2) +
  ggtitle("") +
  xlab(labs_C[1]) +
  ylab(labs_C[2]) +
  theme_bw()

# Permanova
META_C <- as.data.frame(META_C)
vegan::adonis2(dist_C ~ district_cat + classif, by = "margin", data = META_C, permutations = 9999)
```

### 12.7.2 Species level
```{r}
phy_sp_C = tax_glom(physeq_child, taxrank = "Species")
phy_ra_sp_C <- transform_sample_counts(phy_sp_C, function(x) x / sum(x)) 

OTU_C = as(otu_table(phy_ra_sp_C), "matrix")
otu_C <- as.data.frame(OTU_C)
TAX_C = as(tax_table(phy_ra_sp_C), "matrix")
tax_C <- as.data.frame(TAX_C)
META_C = as(sample_data(phy_ra_sp_C), "matrix")
meta_C <- as.data.frame(META_C)

tax_otu_C <- cbind(tax_C, otu_C)
tax_otu_C$Name <- str_c(tax_otu_C$Kingdom, '_',tax_otu_C$Phylum, '_', tax_otu_C$Class, '_', tax_otu_C$Order, '_', tax_otu_C$Family, '_', tax_otu_C$Genus, '_', tax_otu_C$Species)
n_distinct(tax_otu_C$Name)
tax_otu_C[, 234] <- as.character(tax_otu_C[, 234])
length(unique(tax_otu_C[,234]))
rownames(tax_otu_C) <- tax_otu_C[,234]
tax_otu_C <- tax_otu_C[,-c(1:8,234)]
tax_otu_C <- t(tax_otu_C)
class(tax_otu_C) <- "numeric"
tax_otu_C <- as.data.frame(tax_otu_C)
dist_C <- vegdist(tax_otu_C[, 1:2271],  method = "bray")
PCOA_C <- pcoa(dist_C)
vectorPCOA_C <- cbind(PCOA_C$vectors[, 1:2])

# Arrows and taxa name
env.fit_sp_C <- envfit(vectorPCOA_C, tax_otu_C[,1:2271], perm = 999) #Warning: the standard deviation is zero

env.fit_C.sig  <- as.data.frame(scores(env.fit_sp_C, display = "vectors"))
env.fit_C.vect <- as.list(env.fit_sp_C$vectors)
coordinates_C <- cbind(as.data.frame(env.fit_C.vect$arrows*sqrt(env.fit_C.vect$r)), as.data.frame(env.fit_C.vect$pvals))
coordinates_sign_C <- subset(coordinates_C, as.data.frame(env.fit_C.vect$pvals) <= 0.05)
coordinates_sign_C <- cbind(coordinates_sign_C, species = rownames(coordinates_sign_C))
arr_pvals_coord_C <- coordinates_sign_C %>%
  mutate(Coord = (Axis.1*Axis.1)+(Axis.2*Axis.2))
arr_pvals_coord_C[,5] <- as.numeric(arr_pvals_coord_C[,5])
df_envfit_C <- scores(env.fit_sp_C,display=c("vectors"))
df_envfit_C <- df_envfit_C*vegan:::ordiArrowMul(df_envfit_C)

df_envfit_C <- as.data.frame(df_envfit_C)
df_envfit_C <- df_envfit_C %>%
  dplyr::mutate(arrow_length = sqrt(Axis.1^2 + Axis.2^2))
df_envfit_C$species <- rownames(df_envfit_C)
df_envfit_C <- df_envfit_C %>%
  arrange(desc(arrow_length)) %>%
  slice(1:3)
rownames(df_envfit_C) = df_envfit_C$species
df_envfit_C = df_envfit_C[,-3]

df_envfit_C <- df_envfit_C %>% 
  filter(species %in% coordinates_sign_C$species)
arrows_names_C <- str_split_fixed(df_envfit_C$species, "_", 7)
arrows_names_C <- as.data.frame(arrows_names_C)
arrows_names_C <- arrows_names_C %>%
  mutate(tax_name = case_when(!str_detect(V7, "Unassigned") ~ V7,
                              !str_detect(V6, "Unassigned") ~ paste(V6, V7),
                              !str_detect(V5, "Unassigned") ~ paste(V5, V7),
                              !str_detect(V4, "Unassigned") ~ paste(V4, V7),
                              !str_detect(V3, "Unassigned") ~ paste(V3, V7),
                              str_detect(V3, "Unassigned") ~ paste(V3, V7),
                              TRUE ~ V7
                              ))
df_envfit_C <- df_envfit_C %>% 
  mutate(tax_name = arrows_names_C$tax_name)

# Plotting
ft.scores_C <- as.data.frame(vectorPCOA_C)
ft.scores_C$fastqID <- rownames(tax_otu_C)
which(rownames(meta_C) != rownames(ft.scores_C))


ft.scores_C$classif <- meta_C$classif
ft.scores_C$howborn <- meta_C$howborn
ft.scores_C$district_cat <- meta_C$district_cat
ft.scores_C <- distinct(ft.scores_C)

per_explained_C <- 100*PCOA_C$values$Relative_eig / sum(PCOA_C$values$Relative_eig)
per_explained_C <- round(per_explained_C[1:2], digits = 1)
labs_C <- c(glue("Axis1 [{per_explained_C[1]}%]"),
          glue("Axis2 [{per_explained_C[2]}%]"))

# Define thresholds (10% from edges) to avoid having the labels out of frame
x_min <- min(df_envfit_C$Axis.1)
x_max <- max(df_envfit_C$Axis.1)
y_min <- min(df_envfit_C$Axis.2)
y_max <- max(df_envfit_C$Axis.2)

df_envfit_C <- df_envfit_C %>%
  mutate(edge_label = Axis.1 < x_min + 0.1*(x_max-x_min) |
                       Axis.1 > x_max - 0.1*(x_max-x_min) |
                       Axis.2 < y_min + 0.1*(y_max-y_min) |
                       Axis.2 > y_max - 0.1*(y_max-y_min))


ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = ft.scores_C,
             aes(x = Axis.1, y = Axis.2,
                 color = howborn, shape = district_cat),
             size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal_howborn, name = "Mode of delivery") +
  scale_shape_manual(limits = c("Rural", "Urban"),
                     values=c(15, 16), name = "District") +
  geom_segment(aes(x=0, y=0,
                   xend=df_envfit_C$Axis.1*0.5,
                   yend=df_envfit_C$Axis.2*0.5),
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm")),
               color="#808080", alpha=0.5) +
  geom_text_repel(data = df_envfit_C %>% filter(edge_label),
                  aes(x = Axis.1*0.52, y = Axis.2*0.52, label = tax_name),
                  size = 3,
                  color = "#303030",
                  fontface = 3,
                  max.overlaps = Inf,
                  segment.alpha = 0.3
                  ) +
  geom_text(data = df_envfit_C %>% filter(!edge_label),
            aes(x = Axis.1*0.52, y = Axis.2*0.52, label = tax_name),
            size = 3,
            color = "#303030",
            fontface = 3
            ) +
  xlab(labs_C[1]) +
  ylab(labs_C[2]) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

# Permanova
vegan::adonis2(dist_C ~ district_cat, data = meta_C, permutations = 9999) # howborn + district_cat, by = "margin"
```

# 14. Heat map of the children's microbiome according to the maternal nutritional status
## 14.1 Create one dataframe per nutritional category with the mean abundance per taxa
```{r}
# Normally nourished children (nn)
  physeq_C_nn_gen <- subset_samples(phy_ra_gen, individual == "Child" & classif == "Normally nourished") # Change here which taxonomic level is wanted
  # Calculate the prevalence of each taxon
  prevdf_C_nn_gen = apply(X = otu_table(physeq_C_nn_gen), 
                        MARGIN = ifelse(taxa_are_rows(physeq_C_nn_gen),
                                        yes = 1, no = 2), FUN = function(x){sum(x>0)}) 
  #Create a data frame with prevalence and abundance information
  prevdf_C_nn_gen = data.frame(Prevalence_Normo = prevdf_C_nn_gen, 
                             Percentage_Prev_Normo = 100*prevdf_C_nn_gen/90, # 90 samples in this dataset (physeq_gen_rel_nn)
                             Mean_Abundance_Normo = 100*taxa_sums(physeq_C_nn_gen)/90, # 90 samples in this dataset (physeq_gen_rel_nn) => Average relative abundance of each taxon per sample (%)
                             Total_Abundance_Normo = taxa_sums(physeq_C_nn_gen),
                             tax_table(physeq_C_nn_gen)) 
  prevdf_C_nn_gen <- prevdf_C_nn_gen[, -c(11:12)] #at the genus level

# Overnourished children (on)
  physeq_C_on_gen <- subset_samples(phy_ra_gen, individual == "Child" & classif == "Overnourished")
  # Calculate the prevalence of each taxon
  prevdf_C_on_gen = apply(X = otu_table(physeq_C_on_gen), 
                            MARGIN = ifelse(taxa_are_rows(physeq_C_on_gen),
                                            yes = 1, no = 2), FUN = function(x){sum(x>0)}) 
  #Create a data frame with prevalence and abundance information
  prevdf_C_on_gen = data.frame(Prevalence_Over = prevdf_C_on_gen, 
                                 Percentage_Prev_Over = 100*prevdf_C_on_gen/96, # 96 samples in this dataset (physeq_gen_rel_nn)
                                 Mean_Abundance_Over = 100*taxa_sums(physeq_C_on_gen)/96, # 96 samples in this dataset (physeq_gen_rel_nn)
                                 Total_Abundance_Over = taxa_sums(physeq_C_on_gen),
                                 tax_table(physeq_C_on_gen)) 
  prevdf_C_on_gen <- prevdf_C_on_gen[, -c(11:12)]
  
# Undernourished children (un)
  physeq_C_un_gen <- subset_samples(phy_ra_gen, individual == "Child" & classif == "Undernourished")
  # Calculate the prevalence of each taxon
  prevdf_C_un_gen = apply(X = otu_table(physeq_C_un_gen), 
                            MARGIN = ifelse(taxa_are_rows(physeq_C_un_gen),
                                            yes = 1, no = 2), FUN = function(x){sum(x>0)}) 
  #Create a data frame with prevalence and abundance information
  prevdf_C_un_gen = data.frame(Prevalence_Under = prevdf_C_un_gen, 
                                 Percentage_Prev_Under = 100*prevdf_C_un_gen/38, # 38 samples in this dataset (physeq_gen_rel_nn)
                                 Mean_Abundance_Under = 100*taxa_sums(physeq_C_un_gen)/38, # 38 samples in this dataset (physeq_gen_rel_nn)
                                 Total_Abundance_Under = taxa_sums(physeq_C_un_gen),
                                 tax_table(physeq_C_un_gen)) 
  prevdf_C_un_gen <- prevdf_C_un_gen[, -c(11:12)]
  

# Merge the three dataframes (normo, over and under)
  prevdf_gen <- cbind(prevdf_C_nn_gen[,c(1:4)], prevdf_C_on_gen[,c(1:4)], prevdf_C_un_gen)

# Remove unwanted objects  
  rm("prevdf_C_nn_gen", "prevdf_C_on_gen", "prevdf_C_un_gen")
```

## 14.2 Create categories
```{r}
prevdf_gen <- prevdf_gen %>%
  mutate(Intersect_category = "")

# Low prevalence (< 10% prevalence in all categories and > 0%)
prevdf_gen$Intersect_category[which(prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Normo < 10 & prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Normo > 0 &
                                      prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Under < 10 & prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Under > 0 &
                                      prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Over < 10 & prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Over > 0)
                              ] <- "Low prevalence (< 10% prevalence in all categories and > 0%)"

# Middle prevalence (between 10% and 74% prevalence) between the 3 groups
prevdf_gen$Intersect_category[which(prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Normo >= 10 & prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Under >= 10 & prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Over >= 10
                                    & prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Normo < 75 & prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Under < 75 & prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Over < 75)] <- "Middle prevalence (between 10% and 74% prevalence)"

# High prevalence (between 75% and 99% prevalence) between the 3 groups
prevdf_gen$Intersect_category[which(prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Normo >= 75 & prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Under >= 75 & prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Over >= 75
                                    & prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Normo < 100 & prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Under < 100 & prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Over < 102)] <- "High prevalence (between 75% and 99% prevalence)"

# Full prevalence between the 3 groups
prevdf_gen$Intersect_category[which(prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Normo >= 100 & prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Under >= 100 & prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Over >= 100)] <- "Omnipresent"

table(prevdf_gen$Intersect_category)

# Uniquely Normally nourished
prevdf_gen$Intersect_category[which(prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Normo > 0
                                    & prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Under == 0 
                                    & prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Over == 0)] <- "Uniquely Normally nourished"

# Uniquely Undernourished
prevdf_gen$Intersect_category[which(prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Under > 0
                                    & prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Over == 0
                                    & prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Normo == 0)] <- "Uniquely Undernourished"

# Uniquely Overnourished
prevdf_gen$Intersect_category[which(prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Over > 0
                                    & prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Under == 0
                                    & prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Normo == 0)] <- "Uniquely Overnourished"

table(prevdf_gen$Intersect_category)

# No pattern
prevdf_gen <- prevdf_gen %>%
  mutate(Intersect_category = ifelse(Intersect_category == "",
                                     "No pattern",
                                     Intersect_category)
         )

table(prevdf_gen$Intersect_category)


# Order the categories
prevdf_gen$Intersect_category <- as.factor(prevdf_gen$Intersect_category)
prevdf_gen$Intersect_category <- factor(prevdf_gen$Intersect_category, levels=c("Uniquely Normally nourished", "Uniquely Undernourished", "Uniquely Overnourished",
                                                                                "Low prevalence (< 10% prevalence in all categories and > 0%)",
                                                                                "Middle prevalence (between 10% and 74% prevalence)",
                                                                                "High prevalence (between 75% and 99% prevalence)",
                                                                                "Omnipresent",
                                                                                "No pattern"),
                                        ordered = TRUE)

table(prevdf_gen$Intersect_category)

# Modify taxonomy to add the latest taxonomically assigned taxa
prevdf_gen <- prevdf_gen %>%
  mutate(Genus = case_when(!str_detect(Genus, "GGB") ~ Genus,
                           !str_detect(Family, "FGB") ~ paste(Family, Genus),
                           !str_detect(Order, "OFGB") ~ paste(Order, Genus),
                           !str_detect(Class, "CFGB") ~ paste(Class, Genus),
                           str_detect(Class, "CFGB") ~ paste(Phylum, Genus),
                           TRUE ~ Genus
                           ))
    
# Identify rows where all three columns are equal to 0 and remove them
    rows_all_zero <- prevdf_gen[prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Normo == 0 &
                                  prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Over  == 0 &
                                  prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Under == 0,
                                ] # 895 empty taxon
    
    cols <- c("Percentage_Prev_Normo", "Percentage_Prev_Over", "Percentage_Prev_Under")
    prevdf_gen <- prevdf_gen %>%
      filter(rowSums(across(all_of(cols))) != 0) # 1178 - 895 = 283

table(prevdf_gen$Intersect_category)

# Order the dataframe by Intersect_category
    prevdf_gen_ordered <- prevdf_gen[order(prevdf_gen$Intersect_category, -prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Normo, prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Over,
                                           prevdf_gen$Percentage_Prev_Under),]
    
    prevdf_gen_hm <- prevdf_gen_ordered # create another one for heat map that will have the modifications
    rownames(prevdf_gen_hm) <- make.unique(prevdf_gen_hm$Genus)
      
# Take only the mean abundances for the 3 categories and transpose the matrix
    hm_tab <- t(prevdf_gen_hm[,c(3, 7, 11)])
    rownames(hm_tab)[1] <- "Normally nourished"
    rownames(hm_tab)[2] <- "Overnourished"
    rownames(hm_tab)[3] <- "Undernourished"
```

## 14.3 Construct the heatmap
```{r}
# Colors
range(hm_tab, na.rm = TRUE)
quantile(unlist(hm_tab), c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)

hm_long <- hm_tab %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("group") %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -group,
               names_to = "Taxon",
               values_to = "Abundance"
               ) %>%
  filter(Abundance > 0)   # remove all zeros (all cases where the taxon is not present in a classif group)


#pdf("Hist_prev_sp_C_density.pdf", height = 5, width = 5)
ggplot(hm_long, aes(x = Abundance, color = group, fill = group)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.3) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_color_manual(name = NULL,
                     values = pal_muac
                     ) +
  scale_fill_manual(name = NULL,
                    values = pal_muac
                    ) +
  labs(x = "Mean relative abundance per taxon (log10 scale)",
       y = "Number of taxa"
       ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.title = element_blank()
        )
#dev.off()

comparisons <- list(
  c("Normally nourished", "Overnourished"),
  c("Normally nourished", "Undernourished"),
  c("Overnourished", "Undernourished")
)

ggplot(hm_long, aes(x = group, y = Abundance, color = group, fill = group)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.3, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_color_manual(name = NULL, values = pal_muac) +
  scale_fill_manual(name = NULL, values = pal_muac) +
  labs(x = NULL,
       y = "Mean relative abundance per taxon (log10 scale)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        plot.title = element_blank()) +
  ggpubr::stat_compare_means(comparisons = comparisons)
# ggsave("Mean relative abundance per taxon.pdf", width = 5, height = 5)

col_fun = colorRamp2(c(0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 34),c("white", "#FDE725FF", "#B8DE29FF", "#73D055FF","#20A486FF", "#287D8EFF", "#404788FF", "#440154FF"))

# Side annotations
row_annot <- rowAnnotation(ls = prevdf_gen_hm$Intersect_category,
                           col = list(ls=c("Uniquely Normally nourished" = "khaki2",
                                           "Uniquely Undernourished" = "orange2",
                                           "Uniquely Overnourished" = "pink2",

                                           "Omnipresent" = "#440154FF",
                                           "Middle prevalence (between 10% and 74% prevalence)" = "darkcyan",
                                           "High prevalence (between 75% and 99% prevalence)" = "lightblue2",
                                           "No pattern" = "lightgrey")),
                           annotation_label = "Prevalence", 
                           annotation_name_side = "top", 
                           annotation_name_rot = 45)
    
# Split the heat map in segments
table(prevdf_gen_hm$Intersect_category)

split_hm = rep("Uniquely Normally nourished", 283)
split_hm[49:77] = "Uniquely Undernourished"
split_hm[78:128] = "Uniquely Overnourished"
```

```{r}
  group_by(Genus) %>%
  kruskal_test(abundance ~ group) %>%         # Kruskal–Wallis
  left_join(core_test %>%                     # add post-hoc Dunn test
```

```{r}
  prevdf_C_un_sp <- prevdf_C_un_sp[, -12]
  

# Merge the three dataframes (normo, over and under)
  prevdf_sp <- cbind(prevdf_C_nn_sp[,c(1:4)], prevdf_C_on_sp[,c(1:4)], prevdf_C_un_sp)

# Remove unwanted objects  
  rm("physeq_C_nn_sp", "prevdf_C_nn_sp", "physeq_C_on_sp", "prevdf_C_on_sp", "physeq_C_un_sp", "prevdf_C_un_sp")
  
# More than 75% prevalent in all nutritional groups
prevdf_sp = prevdf_sp %>%
  mutate(Core = "No")

prevdf_sp$Core[which(prevdf_sp$Percentage_Prev_Normo >= 75 & prevdf_sp$Percentage_Prev_Under >= 75 & prevdf_sp$Percentage_Prev_Over >= 75)] <- "Yes"

table(prevdf_sp$Core)
```

# 16. Clustering of the children's microbiomes at the species level
### 16.1 Prep data: get otu_table
```{r}
physeq_abs_sp_C <- subset_samples(phy_abs_sp, individual == "Child")
#physeq_ra_sp_C <- subset_samples(phy_ra_sp, individual == "Child")
otu_table_sp_C = as.data.frame(otu_table(physeq_abs_sp_C))
otu_table_sp_C = rev(otu_table_sp_C) #put the first column as C1WST001 and not C1WST269 (mirror horizontally the data frame)

# Get the species names as row names (from tax table)
otu_table_sp_C$ASV_abs = rownames(otu_table_sp_C)
otu_table_sp_C = left_join(otu_table_sp_C, tax_names_abs_df, by = "ASV_abs")
otu_table_sp_C = otu_table_sp_C[,-234] #remove the last column = SGB
otu_table_sp_C = otu_table_sp_C[,-c(226:232)] #remove the taxonomy columns except "species"
rownames(otu_table_sp_C) = otu_table_sp_C$Species
otu_table_sp_C = otu_table_sp_C[, -226] #remove the species column
otu_table_sp_C = as.data.frame(t(otu_table_sp_C))

# Order species from most abundant to least abundant
otu_table_sp_C = otu_table_sp_C[,order(colSums(otu_table_sp_C), decreasing = TRUE)]

# Transform in relative abundances
otu_table_sp_C_ra = apply(otu_table_sp_C, 1, function(x) 100*x/sum(x))
otu_table_sp_C_ra = as.data.frame(t(otu_table_sp_C_ra))

# Remove unnecessary files
rm("otu_table_sp_C")
```

### 16.2 Distance matrix and clustering into 2 clusters
```{r}
# Create a distance matrix of samples
dist_eu_sp_C = vegdist(otu_table_sp_C_ra, method = "euclidean")
dist_br_sp_C = vegdist(otu_table_sp_C_ra, method = "bray")

# Create clustering (samples 2 by 2)
hc_eu_sp = hclust(dist_eu_sp_C, method = "ward.D2")
hc_br_sp = hclust(dist_br_sp_C, method = "ward.D2")

# Create dendrogram (=~ phylogenetic tree)
dend_eu_sp = as.dendrogram(hc_eu_sp)
plot(dend_eu_sp)
dend_br_sp = as.dendrogram(hc_br_sp)
plot(dend_br_sp)

# Assess where to cut the dendrogram and thus how many clusters is the optimum to highlight the differences 
# NbClust(data = otu_table_sp_C_ra,
#         diss = dist_eu_sp_C,
#         distance = NULL,
#         min.nc = 2,
#         max.nc = 10,
#         method = "ward.D2",
#         index = "ch")
#tells you how many clusters are best between 2 and 10 => the best number here is 2

# NbClust(data = otu_table_sp_C_ra,
#         diss = dist_br_sp_C,
#         distance = NULL,
#         min.nc = 2,
#         max.nc = 10,
#         method = "ward.D2",
#         index = "ch")
#With Bray distance, the optimal nbr of clusters is also 2

# Defines the clusters according to the index calculated above
nClrs = 2
clrs_eu_sp = cutree(hc_eu_sp, k=nClrs)
clrs_br_sp = cutree(hc_br_sp, k=nClrs)

table(clrs_eu_sp)
table(clrs_br_sp)

clusters_eu_sp = as.data.frame(clrs_eu_sp)
clusters_eu_sp = clusters_eu_sp %>%
  mutate(Sample = rownames(clusters_eu_sp)) 

clusters_br_sp = as.data.frame(clrs_br_sp)
clusters_br_sp = clusters_br_sp %>%
  mutate(Sample = rownames(clusters_br_sp))

cluster_check = left_join(clusters_eu_sp, clusters_br_sp, by = "Sample")
cluster_check_diff <- cluster_check %>%
  filter(clrs_br_sp != clrs_eu_sp)
#There is only one sample (C1WST094) which changes cluster depending on the distance method (Bray Curtis or euclidean) used. As it does not make a huge difference, I will continue using the euclidean method.
rm("dist_br_sp_C", "hc_br_sp", "dend_br_sp", "clrs_br_sp", "clusters_br_sp", "cluster_check", "cluster_check_diff")
  
clusters_sp = data.frame(cluster = ifelse(test = clrs_eu_sp == 1, yes = "Cluster 1", no = "Cluster 2")) #replace numeric values with string name

# Extract metadata of the phyloseq object and add cluster
metaHM = as.data.frame(as.matrix(sample_data(physeq_abs_sp_C)))
clusters_sp$NovogeneID = rownames(clusters_sp)
metaHM = merge(metaHM, clusters_sp, by = "NovogeneID")
rownames(metaHM) = metaHM$NovogeneID

#add clusters to phyloseq object
metadata_df = metadata_df %>%
    select(-cluster) #remove the currrent "cluster" column in case it was already added
metadata_df = left_join(metadata_df, clusters_sp, by = "NovogeneID")
metadata = sample_data(metadata_df) #replace the previous metadata phyloseq with the new one with the column cluster
rownames(metadata) <- metadata$NovogeneID
sample_data(phy_abs_sp) <- sample_data(metadata)
sample_data(physeq_ra_filt) <- sample_data(metadata)

```

### 16.3  Variables explaining the 2 clusters
```{r}
  i1_clrs_1 = metadata_df$i1[metadata_df$cluster %in% c("Cluster 1", "Cluster 1")] # get the i1 for which cluster = 1 has been attributed to the child 
  i1_clrs_2 = metadata_df$i1[metadata_df$cluster %in% c("Cluster 2", "Cluster 2")] # get the i1 for which cluster = 2 has been attributed to the child 
  
  metadata_df_clrs <- metadata_df %>%
    mutate(cluster = case_when(
      individual == "Mother" & i1 %in% i1_clrs_1 ~ "Cluster 1",

    ))
  
# Gtsummary

        by = "cluster", #classif, clusters etc (categorie)
        missing_text = "NA",
        #missing = "no",
        statistic = list(all_continuous() ~ "{mean} ({min}-{max})")
      ) %>%
        add_overall(last = TRUE) %>%
        add_p() %>%
        bold_labels()
```
  

## 16.10 Variables explaining the 6 clusters
```{r}
table(metadata_df$cluster_extend)

# I need to copy the cluster group info of the child to his/her mother on both preg and 1wpp lines, to be able to do the gtsummary of maternal variables.
  i1_clrs_1 = metadata_df$i1[metadata_df$cluster_extend %in% c("Cluster 1", "Cluster 1")] # get the i1 for which cluster = 1 has been attributed to the child 
  i1_clrs_2 = metadata_df$i1[metadata_df$cluster_extend %in% c("Cluster 2", "Cluster 2")] # get the i1 for which cluster = 2 has been attributed to the child 
  i1_clrs_3 = metadata_df$i1[metadata_df$cluster_extend %in% c("Cluster 3", "Cluster 3")] # get the i1 for which cluster = 3 has been attributed to the child 
  i1_clrs_4 = metadata_df$i1[metadata_df$cluster_extend %in% c("Cluster 4", "Cluster 4")] # get the i1 for which cluster = 4 has been attributed to the child 
  i1_clrs_5 = metadata_df$i1[metadata_df$cluster_extend %in% c("Cluster 5", "Cluster 5")] # get the i1 for which cluster = 5 has been attributed to the child 
  i1_clrs_6 = metadata_df$i1[metadata_df$cluster_extend %in% c("Cluster 6", "Cluster 6")] # get the i1 for which cluster = 6 has been attributed to the child 

  metadata_df_clrs <- metadata_df %>%
    mutate(cluster_extend = case_when(individual == "Mother" & i1 %in% i1_clrs_1 ~ "Cluster 1",
                                      individual == "Mother" & i1 %in% i1_clrs_2 ~ "Cluster 2",
                                      individual == "Mother" & i1 %in% i1_clrs_3 ~ "Cluster 3",
                                      individual == "Mother" & i1 %in% i1_clrs_4 ~ "Cluster 4",
                                      individual == "Mother" & i1 %in% i1_clrs_5 ~ "Cluster 5",
                                      individual == "Mother" & i1 %in% i1_clrs_6 ~ "Cluster 6",
                                      TRUE ~ cluster_extend  # Keep the original cluster value if no conditions are met
                                      ))
  
  table(metadata_df_clrs$cluster_extend)
  
# I need to create one variables (yes/no) per cluster to be able to do chi2/Fisher tests with gtsummary, otherwise nothing will be significant (comparing 2 distributions instead of a chi2 table is not great)
 metadata_df_clrs <- metadata_df_clrs %>%
   mutate(cluster1 = if_else(cluster_extend == "Cluster 1", "Yes", "No"),
          cluster2 = if_else(cluster_extend == "Cluster 2", "Yes", "No"),
          cluster3 = if_else(cluster_extend == "Cluster 3", "Yes", "No"),
          cluster4 = if_else(cluster_extend == "Cluster 4", "Yes", "No"),
          cluster5 = if_else(cluster_extend == "Cluster 5", "Yes", "No"),
          cluster6 = if_else(cluster_extend == "Cluster 6", "Yes", "No")
          )
  
 table(metadata_df_clrs$cluster1)
 
# Gtsummary
  metadata_df_clrs %>%
    filter(individual == "Child") %>%
    filter(Visit == "W1") %>%
      gtsummary::tbl_summary(
        include = c(agechild), #, lddm, age, twin, prepregbmi_cat, bf2, obc, s90, s91c, district_cat, howborn_combined
        by = "cluster1",
```

## 16.11 Clustering of the maternal stool microbiome and correlation with babies clustering
```{r}
physeq_abs_sp_M <- subset_samples(phy_abs_sp, individual == "Mother" & Visit == "Inc")
#physeq_ra_sp_M <- subset_samples(phy_ra_sp, individual == "Mother")
otu_table_sp_M = as.data.frame(otu_table(physeq_abs_sp_M))
otu_table_sp_M = rev(otu_table_sp_M) #put the first column as MPST001 and not MPST269 (mirror horizontally the data frame)

# Get the species names as row names (from tax table)
otu_table_sp_M$ASV_abs = rownames(otu_table_sp_M)
otu_table_sp_M = left_join(otu_table_sp_M, tax_names_abs_df, by = "ASV_abs")
otu_table_sp_M = otu_table_sp_M[,-254] #remove the last column = SGB
otu_table_sp_M = otu_table_sp_M[,-c(246:252)] #remove the taxonomy columns except "species"
rownames(otu_table_sp_M) = otu_table_sp_M$Species
otu_table_sp_M = otu_table_sp_M[, -246] #remove the species column
otu_table_sp_M = as.data.frame(t(otu_table_sp_M))

# Order species from most abundant to least abundant
otu_table_sp_M = otu_table_sp_M[,order(colSums(otu_table_sp_M), decreasing = TRUE)]

# Transform in relative abundances
otu_table_sp_M_ra = apply(otu_table_sp_M, 1, function(x) 100*x/sum(x))
otu_table_sp_M_ra = as.data.frame(t(otu_table_sp_M_ra))

# Remove unnecessary files
rm("otu_table_sp_M")


# Distance matrix and clustering into x clusters
# Create a distance matrix of samples
dist_eu_sp_M = vegdist(otu_table_sp_M_ra, method = "euclidean")

# Create clustering (samples 2 by 2)
hc_eu_sp_M = hclust(dist_eu_sp_M, method = "ward.D2")

# Create dendrogram (=~ phylogenetic tree)
dend_eu_sp_M = as.dendrogram(hc_eu_sp_M)
plot(dend_eu_sp_M)

# Assess where to cut the dendrogram and thus how many clusters is the optimum to highlight the differences 
# NbClust(data = otu_table_sp_M_ra,
#         diss = dist_eu_sp_M,
#         distance = NULL,
#         min.nc = 2,
#         max.nc = 10,
#         method = "ward.D2",
#         index = "ch")
# tells you how many clusters are best between 2 and 10 => the best number here is 2

# Defines the clusters according to the index calculated above
nClrs = 2
clrs_eu_sp_M = cutree(hc_eu_sp_M, k=nClrs)

table(clrs_eu_sp_M)

clusters_eu_sp_M = as.data.frame(clrs_eu_sp_M)
clusters_eu_sp_M = clusters_eu_sp_M %>%
  mutate(Sample = rownames(clusters_eu_sp_M)) 
  
clusters_sp_M = data.frame(cluster_M = ifelse(test = clrs_eu_sp_M == 1, yes = "Cluster 1", no = "Cluster 2")) #replace numeric values with string name

# Extract metadata of the phyloseq object and add cluster
metaHM = as.data.frame(as.matrix(sample_data(physeq_abs_sp_M)))
clusters_sp_M$NovogeneID = rownames(clusters_sp_M)
metaHM = merge(metaHM, clusters_sp_M, by = "NovogeneID")
rownames(metaHM) = metaHM$NovogeneID

# Add clusters to phyloseq object
metadata_df = metadata_df %>%
    select(-cluster_M) #remove the currrent "cluster_M" column in case it was already added
metadata_df = left_join(metadata_df, clusters_sp_M, by = "NovogeneID")
metadata = sample_data(metadata_df) #replace the previous metadata phyloseq with the new one with the column cluster
rownames(metadata) <- metadata$NovogeneID
sample_data(phy_abs_sp) <- sample_data(metadata)
sample_data(physeq_ra_filt) <- sample_data(metadata)


# Test the association between the maternal clustering and the children clustering
cluster_ass = metadata_df %>%
  select(individual, Visit, VG_ID, cluster, cluster_M, cluster_extend) %>%
  filter(!(individual == "Mother" & Visit == "W1"))

cluster_child <- cluster_ass %>%
  filter(individual == "Child") %>%
  select(VG_ID, cluster, cluster_extend)

cluster_mother <- cluster_ass %>%
  filter(individual == "Mother") %>%
  select(VG_ID, cluster_M)

cluster_final <- cluster_child %>%
  left_join(cluster_mother, by = "VG_ID") %>%
  select(VG_ID, cluster, cluster_M, cluster_extend)


table(cluster_final$cluster, cluster_final$cluster_M)

chisq.test(table(cluster_final$cluster, cluster_final$cluster_M)) 
fisher.test(table(cluster_final$cluster, cluster_final$cluster_M)) 

# For extended clusters
tab <- table(cluster_final$cluster_M, cluster_final$cluster_extend)
tab
fisher.test(tab)
chisq.test(tab)
```

```{r}
# Convert the distance matrix to a long format data frame
dist_eu_sp_C_m = as.matrix(dist_eu_sp_C)

# Create a consistent identifier for each pair of samples
dist_eu_sp_C_df$id <- apply(dist_eu_sp_C_df, 1, function(row) {

})
```

# 19. Exploration of the bifidobacterium co-exclusion
```{r}
# Subset the dataset for bifidobacterium in children samples. Remove samples which do not contain any bifido
bifido_ra_sp = abun_table_ra_df %>%
  filter(Genus == "Bifidobacterium") %>%
  select(-starts_with("M")) %>%
  select(where(~ !all(.x == 0))) 

# Remove "Bifidobacterium" from Species name to have a cleaner graph later
bifido_ra_sp <- bifido_ra_sp %>%
  mutate(Species = str_replace(Species, "^Bifidobacterium_", "B. "),
         Species = str_replace(Species, "_", " ")
         ) %>%
  column_to_rownames("Species")

# Keep only the abundances
bifido_ra <- bifido_ra_sp %>% 
  select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  filter(rowSums(select(., where(is.numeric))) > 0) # remove the species row if it is not present in any children's sample

bifido_ra_t <- t(bifido_ra)

# Test for correlation
cor_mat <- cor(bifido_ra_t, method = "spearman") #Spearman → best for microbiome (non-normal, zeros)

library(corrplot)
rcorr_res <- Hmisc::rcorr(as.matrix(bifido_ra_t), type = "spearman")

cor_mat  <- rcorr_res$r
p_mat    <- rcorr_res$P

corrplot(cor_mat, 
         p.mat = p_mat, 
         sig.level = 0.05,
         type = "upper",
         method = "circle",
         tl.col = "black",
         addCoef.col = "black",
         number.cex = .5,
         diag = FALSE)

  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("Species1") %>%

  filter(Species1 < Species2) %>%   # avoid duplicates

sp2 <- "B. longum"
sp3 <- "B. breve"

  tibble::rownames_to_column("Sample")

)

  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red", fill = "red", alpha = 0.2) +
  stat_cor(method = "spearman",
           label.x.npc = "left",
           label.y.npc = "top") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = sp1,
       y = sp3) +
  theme(axis.title = element_text(face = "italic"))
```

# 21. Maternal and children species/SGB overlap
```{r}
# Identify maternal (MPST) and child (C1WST) column names
maternal_cols <- grep("^MPST", colnames(abun_table_ra_df), value = TRUE)
child_cols <- grep("^C1WST", colnames(abun_table_ra_df), value = TRUE)

# The last 8 columns are taxonomy
taxa_cols <- tail(colnames(abun_table_ra_df), 8)

# Check overlap at the Species level
species_overlap <- abun_table_ra_df %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Species) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(in_mothers = any(rowSums(dplyr::select(cur_data(), all_of(maternal_cols)) > 0) > 0), # A species is present if any row belonging to it has abundance > 0
            in_children = any(rowSums(dplyr::select(cur_data(), all_of(child_cols)) > 0) > 0)
            ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Species)) # Remove any potential NA species rows

# Species in children that ARE also found in mothers
sum(species_overlap$in_children == TRUE & species_overlap$in_mothers == TRUE)
# 500/724 species in infants overlap with mothers

# Species in children that ARE NOT found in mothers
sum(species_overlap$in_children == TRUE & species_overlap$in_mothers == FALSE)
# 224/724 species in infants do not overlap with mothers and come from somewhere else


# Check overlap at the SGB level
SGB_overlap <- abun_table_ra_df %>%
  dplyr::group_by(SGB) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(in_mothers = any(rowSums(dplyr::select(cur_data(), all_of(maternal_cols)) > 0) > 0),
            in_children = any(rowSums(dplyr::select(cur_data(), all_of(child_cols)) > 0) > 0)
            ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(SGB))

# Species in children that ARE also found in mothers
sum(SGB_overlap$in_children == TRUE & SGB_overlap$in_mothers == TRUE)
# 534/783 SGB in infants overlap with mothers

# Species in children that ARE NOT found in mothers
sum(SGB_overlap$in_children == TRUE & SGB_overlap$in_mothers == FALSE)
# 249/783 SGB in infants do not overlap with mothers and come from somewhere else
```

# 22. Relative abundance in maternal samples of specific taxa
```{r}
# Replace "Bifidobacterium_longum" with my species of interest
target_species_1 <- "Bifidobacterium_breve"
target_species_2 <- "Klebsiella_pneumoniae"
target_species_3 <- "Escherichia_coli"


mean_abundance <- abun_table_ra_df %>%
  filter(Species == target_species_3) %>% # Filter for the specific species
  dplyr::select(starts_with("MPST")) %>% # Select only the maternal sample columns (MPSTxxx)
  rowMeans() %>% # Calculate the mean across all these columns. rowMeans is used here because the species might exist in multiple rows (e.g., different SGBs)
  mean() # Final mean across any multiple rows found

cat("Mean abundance of", target_species, "in mothers:", mean_abundance, "\n")

min_val <- min(abun_table_ra_df[, maternal_cols], na.rm = TRUE)
max_val <- max(abun_table_ra_df[, maternal_cols], na.rm = TRUE)

cat("Maternal Abundance Range:", min_val, "to", max_val)

# Pivot maternal data to a long format for plotting
maternal_long <- abun_table_ra_df %>%
  dplyr::select(starts_with("MPST")) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "Sample", values_to = "Abundance")

# Plot the distribution
ggplot(maternal_long, aes(x = Abundance)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Maternal Microbial Abundances",
       x = "Relative Abundance",
       y = "Frequency")

low_abundance_pct <- mean(maternal_long$Abundance < 0.1) * 100
cat("Percentage of observations < 0.1% abundance:", round(low_abundance_pct, 2), "%")
```
